question: A square matrix $A$ of order $3$ satisfies $|A|=-2$. Find $|\operatorname{adj}A|$ and write the matrix $A(\operatorname{adj}A)$.
explanation:
Determinant of the adjoint
For a square matrix of order $n$, $$|\operatorname{adj}A|=|A|^{n-1}$$
Substitution of the order and determinant
Here, $n=3$ and $|A|=-2$. Therefore, $$|\operatorname{adj}A|=(-2)^2=4$$
Adjoint identity
Using $$A(\operatorname{adj}A)=|A|I,$$ we obtain $$A(\operatorname{adj}A)=-2I=\begin{bmatrix}-2&0&0\\0&-2&0\\0&0&-2\end{bmatrix}$$
